pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is the weakest point and is driven mainly by lower earnings, with net debt also higher. Net debt rose by USD 138.6 million in nine months while trailing reported EBITDA fell to USD 360.8 million, so net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 4.89x at the end of FY2025 to 7.76x and on adjusted EBITDA from 4.08x to 5.21x. No pro forma adjustment for the October 2026 credit amendment is established, because that amendment takes effect only at the merger closing. Because the covenant levels are not printed, how much of the revolver stays usable without the relief is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

Cash flow is seasonal and less weak than the nine-month figure suggests. Free cash flow was negative at USD 36.9 million in the nine months of 2026, yet FY2025 free cash flow was USD 247.9 million and trailing free cash flow is USD 221.5 million, because the fourth quarter of 2025 alone produced about USD 321.2 million of operating cash flow as working capital reversed. The first nine months absorbed a Shintech payment of about USD 114 million, so the fourth quarter of 2026 decides whether the pattern repeats, and the issuer guides the fourth quarter lower than the third. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25 and 45

Liquidity is adequate until the covenant relief period ends. Cash of USD 214.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 1,029.6 million total USD 1,244.4 million against USD 1,134.3 million of debt due through 2029, and nothing falls due before November 2027. The receivables facility has only USD 34.0 million of spare capacity limited by its borrowing base, so it is not a reserve, and the revolver and the term loan both mature in March 2030. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C10; calculation C11

The test is the end of covenant relief, no later than 2027-09-30. The credit agreement carries a net leverage ceiling and an interest coverage floor that were relaxed in February 2026, and the ratio levels are not printed, so the headroom cannot be measured; the issuer states compliance and no borrowing limit at 2026-09-30. If the merger closes in the first quarter of 2027 the new facility replaces these terms, so the merger is the planned way past the cliff, and a delay would leave tighter covenants against leverage above the FY2025 level. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9 and 13–14

Earnings concentration is moving from chemicals to Winchester. Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls was 47.85% of nine-month sales against 55.28% a year earlier, its sales fell 14.17% and its segment earnings fell USD 190.6 million, with the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage costing USD 72.2 million, while Winchester sales rose 14.14% against an order backlog of USD 1,331 million. Winchester therefore props up cash flow while commodity chemical pricing stays weak, but about 13% of FY2025 sales are to the U.S. government and the fourth quarter is seasonally weakest. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15

Governance and financial policy are average, with no sponsor. The dividend of USD 0.20 per share a quarter continues, repurchases are not printed for 2026 and USD 1,948.9 million of authority remains, so the board can restart distributions at any time while leverage is elevated. Ratings are Fitch BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, Moody's Ba2 with a Negative outlook and Standard & Poor's BB on Credit Watch Developing, a split that followed the merger announcement. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–53

runs.text: The main credit strength is liquidity and maturity structure. Cash and the undrawn revolver of USD 1,244.4 million cover the first maturity, a USD 465.0 million receivables facility due in 2027, about 2.68x, and the revolver, term loan and 2030 notes fall due in 2030 or later, so refinancing pressure arrives only after the covenant relief and merger milestones. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–14

A second strength is Winchester, whose nine-month sales rose 14.14%, whose segment earnings rose to USD 77.1 million from USD 67.1 million and whose backlog of USD 1,331 million provides visibility, which cushions weak chemical earnings. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C14

A third strength is scale and integration: the largest chlor alkali capacity in North America by the issuer's own account, captive chlorine outlets in epoxy and chlorinated organics, and a diversified product list, which spreads fixed cost and gives more than one outlet for the same electrolysis output. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5 and 14

The main weakness is leverage against falling earnings, with net leverage of 7.76x on reported EBITDA and trailing interest cover of 2.12x, which leaves little room for another outage or price decline. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C9

A second weakness is concentration of operating risk at Freeport and in commodity chemicals, where an outage cost USD 72.2 million in nine months and subsidized Asian competition keeps epoxy and caustic pricing under pressure. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33

A third weakness is cash claims outside the debt and a distribution that does not flex: the Shintech judgment, environmental liabilities of USD 156.8 million and dividends of USD 68.3 million in nine months all call on cash while covenant relief is temporary. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25 and 46

runs.text: The pending transaction is an all-stock merger of equals with Huntsman Corporation under an agreement signed on 2026-06-15 and announced on 2026-06-16. Each Huntsman share converts into a fixed fraction of an Olin share, existing Olin shareholders would own about 54.5% of the combined company and Huntsman stockholders about 45.5%, and Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million. Shareholders of both companies approved on 2026-08-25 and the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired, leaving other regulatory approvals and customary conditions before the expected first quarter of 2027 closing. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8 and 58; EX-99.1_2026-07-30_exhibit991q22026earningspr.htm.jsonl, page 3

On 2026-10-27 Olin signed a second amendment to its senior credit facility that creates a USD 2,500.0 million senior secured facility on the closing date, made up of a USD 750.0 million term loan replacing the existing USD 650.0 million term loan and a USD 1,750.0 million revolver replacing Olin's USD 1,200.0 million revolver and Huntsman's revolver. The new term loan amortises 1.25% a quarter, rising to 1.88% a quarter after the fourth anniversary, the facility matures five years after closing, is guaranteed by certain Huntsman subsidiaries and is secured by first priority liens, and its covenants include a net leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio. No new notes or loans were issued in 2026; in 2025 Olin issued USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2033 and entered the existing senior credit facility to extend maturities. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9 and 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_oln-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Olin's net debt of USD 2,798.3 million is 7.76x trailing reported EBITDA but 5.21x on the issuer's adjusted measure, so creditors depend on covenant relief and liquidity until earnings recover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The gap between the two measures is USD 175.8 million of add-backs over the last twelve months. Trailing interest cover is 2.12x on reported EBITDA. Liquidity of USD 1,244.4 million covers the next maturity, a USD 465.0 million receivables facility due in 2027, but covenant levels are not printed, so headroom is not established.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA, the primary denominator, was USD 544.4 million in FY2025 and USD 360.8 million over the twelve months to 2026-09-30, because nine-month 2026 EBITDA of USD 387.2 million is far below the USD 570.8 million of the same months of 2025. Over the same span net debt rose from USD 2,659.7 million to USD 2,798.3 million, so net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 4.89x to 7.76x and on adjusted EBITDA from 4.08x to 5.21x. The earnings fall is concentrated in Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls, where nine-month segment earnings were USD 80.2 million against USD 270.8 million, helped down by the vinyl chloride monomer outage at Freeport and a smaller hydrogen tax credit. Debt rose because operating cash flow did not cover capital spending, dividends and a distribution to a minority partner, so the revolver and the receivables facility funded the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8; EX-99.1_2026-10-29_exhibit991q32026earningspr.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3 and 8–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_oln-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 21.3 million of restructuring, USD 36.1 million of legacy litigation and USD 24.3 million of merger costs for the nine months of 2026. Restructuring charges appear in every period printed, so they behave as a recurring cost, while merger costs should stop at closing. A creditor who accepts the add-backs sees 5.21x; one who treats restructuring as recurring sees a higher figure, and the annual add-backs for FY2025 are not itemised in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid was USD 129.4 million for the nine months of 2026 against USD 137.1 million a year earlier, and trailing cash interest is USD 170.2 million. Cover on reported EBITDA therefore fell from 3.06x in FY2025 to 2.12x, and on adjusted EBITDA from 3.66x to 3.15x. Falling interest cost does not offset the earnings decline, so cover weakens even as debt costs ease.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 69.7 million for the nine months of 2026 against USD 153.0 million, after a USD 133.4 million receivables build and a USD 81.0 million inventory build. Capital expenditure fell to USD 106.6 million from USD 163.5 million, so free cash flow was negative at USD 36.9 million, and the company still paid USD 68.3 million of dividends with no share repurchases. Net borrowing of USD 185.3 million funded the shortfall, so the dividend is financed with debt while leverage rises.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of USD 214.8 million plus USD 1,029.6 million undrawn on the revolver, down from USD 1,367.2 million at the end of FY2025. The receivables facility had USD 465.0 million drawn and only USD 34.0 million of extra capacity limited by its borrowing base, so it cannot be counted as a reserve. No principal matures in the remainder of 2026 or in 2028; the first call on liquidity is the receivables facility in November 2027, followed by USD 669.3 million of notes in 2029 and USD 1,213.4 million in 2030, when the 2030 notes, the term loan and the revolver all fall due.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit agreement carries a net leverage ceiling and an interest coverage floor, relaxed by the February 2026 amendment until the earlier of 2027-09-30 or the issuer's election, and the issuer states compliance at 2026-09-30 with no limit on borrowing. At FY2025 the leverage test limited additional borrowing to USD 825.3 million, and the ratio levels are not printed, so creditors cannot tell how close the 2026-09-30 position is to the test. The risk is the end of relief, which also releases the guarantees and liens that now secure the credit facility, while leverage on either measure remains above the FY2025 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Huntsman merger is not in these figures. A second credit facility amendment signed on 2026-10-27 provides a USD 2,500.0 million facility only on the closing date, so no net debt effect is recorded at 2026-09-30, and Huntsman's own debt and earnings are not in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for lower risk is that the issuer's own leverage was 4.1x at FY2025 and that fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA is guided to USD 80 million to USD 100 million, against USD 67.7 million implied for the fourth quarter of 2025, which would lift trailing adjusted EBITDA. Normal operations at the vinyl chloride monomer plant were restored in the third quarter, Epoxy turned to a small segment profit and Winchester earnings rose. If trailing adjusted EBITDA recovers toward the FY2025 level, leverage returns near 4x and the view eases; a further decline, or a covenant ceiling close to the current ratio, would harden it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Olin is a widely held, diversified chemicals and ammunition producer with no sponsor, so creditor risk comes from operations, the Shintech judgment and the pending Huntsman merger rather than from shareholder behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chemicals earnings are weak while Winchester carries an order backlog of USD 1,331 million, the dividend continues with negative free cash flow, and the merger, expected in the first quarter of 2027, would replace the credit facility on terms whose combined leverage is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling shareholder or sponsor is disclosed, so governance risk is medium and driven by event exposure, not by extraction. The annual report counts fewer than three thousand record holders, places the beneficial owner table and the board biographies in a proxy statement that is not supplied, and the merger would leave existing Olin shareholders with about 54.5% of the combined company. Sponsor fund life, exit pressure and fee leakage do not apply, but without the proxy statement the absence of a large holder is not confirmed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Winchester is becoming the more reliable earnings leg while chemicals weaken. Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls was 54.34% of FY2025 sales but 47.85% of nine-month 2026 sales, and its nine-month sales fell 14.17% while Winchester sales rose 14.14%. Winchester's backlog of USD 1,331 million, of which 81% is due for delivery in 2026, gives revenue visibility, but about 13% of FY2025 sales are to the U.S. government, whose contracts carry standard termination rights, and the Lake City contract is a single government-owned plant arrangement.

fields.value: Single-site operating risk is concentrated at Freeport, Texas, where outages at the vinyl chloride monomer plant cost chemicals earnings USD 72.2 million in the nine months of 2026 and USD 32.1 million in the third quarter. Management says normal operations were restored in the third quarter. A repeat would hit the largest segment while leverage is already elevated, and the maintenance turnarounds planned for the fourth quarter keep the fourth quarter weaker than the third.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Shintech breach of contract judgment is a cash claim outside the debt. A jury found against Olin on 2026-02-10, Olin recorded charges of USD 75.0 million in the fourth quarter of 2025 and USD 11.1 million in the first quarter of 2026, paid about USD 114 million in the nine months of 2026, and a final judgment was entered on 2026-09-11. Appeal timing is not established, so any further payment is open, and the issuer does not expect material further payments in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation is mixed. Olin paid USD 68.3 million of dividends in the nine months of 2026 against operating cash flow of USD 69.7 million and capital spending of USD 106.6 million, a shortfall of USD 105.2 million that net borrowing funded, and share repurchases are not printed for 2026 after USD 50.5 million in FY2025. USD 1,948.9 million of repurchase authority remains, so a restart is a policy choice the board can make at any time within debt covenants not supplied here.

fields.value: The merger is an all-stock combination in which Huntsman shares convert into new Olin shares; it carries a termination fee of USD 121 million, merger costs of USD 24.3 million in the nine months of 2026 and a USD 2,500.0 million new facility that takes effect only on closing. Both sets of shareholders approved it on 2026-08-25. The new facility replaces Olin's term loan and revolver and Huntsman's revolver, with guarantees from certain Huntsman subsidiaries, so Olin creditors would face a larger obligor whose debt and earnings are not in the supplied documents. Completion timing moved from the first half of 2027 to the first quarter of 2027 between the second and third quarter releases.

Winchester earnings are rising and the Shintech judgment is final at the trial level. The view would ease if the merger closes in the first quarter of 2027 on the stated facility with combined leverage near the issuer's current level, and would harden if closing slips beyond the covenant relief period, which ends no later than 2027-09-30, or if the appeal reverses.

fields.value: The pending transaction is an all-stock merger of equals with Huntsman Corporation under an agreement signed on 2026-06-15 and announced on 2026-06-16. Each Huntsman share converts into a fixed fraction of an Olin share, existing Olin shareholders would own about 54.5% of the combined company and Huntsman stockholders about 45.5%, and Olin could owe a termination fee of USD 121 million. Shareholders of both companies approved on 2026-08-25 and the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period expired, leaving other regulatory approvals and customary conditions before the expected first quarter of 2027 closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On 2026-10-27 Olin signed a second amendment to its senior credit facility that creates a USD 2,500.0 million senior secured facility on the closing date, made up of a USD 750.0 million term loan replacing the existing USD 650.0 million term loan and a USD 1,750.0 million revolver replacing Olin's USD 1,200.0 million revolver and Huntsman's revolver. The new term loan amortises 1.25% a quarter, rising to 1.88% a quarter after the fourth anniversary, the facility matures five years after closing, is guaranteed by certain Huntsman subsidiaries and is secured by first priority liens, and its covenants include a net leverage ratio and an interest coverage ratio. No new notes or loans were issued in 2026; in 2025 Olin issued USD 600.0 million of senior notes due 2033 and entered the existing senior credit facility to extend maturities.

Scope: the fundamental credit assessment of Olin Corporation on its consolidated perimeter, synthesised from the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance work and checked against the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Olin's fundamental credit profile is stretched but liquid, with net leverage of 7.76x on reported EBITDA and 5.21x on adjusted EBITDA, so creditors depend on the 2027 covenant and merger milestones rather than on near-term maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash and the undrawn revolver of USD 1,244.4 million cover the first maturity, a USD 465.0 million receivables facility due in November 2027, about 2.68x, and Winchester earnings are rising. Against that, trailing interest cover on reported EBITDA is only 2.12x and covenant levels are not printed, so the view is a moderate-risk credit with a defined time window, not a distressed one.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the weakest point and is driven mainly by lower earnings, with net debt also higher. Net debt rose by USD 138.6 million in nine months while trailing reported EBITDA fell to USD 360.8 million, so net leverage on reported EBITDA moved from 4.89x at the end of FY2025 to 7.76x and on adjusted EBITDA from 4.08x to 5.21x. No pro forma adjustment for the October 2026 credit amendment is established, because that amendment takes effect only at the merger closing. Because the covenant levels are not printed, how much of the revolver stays usable without the relief is not established.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is seasonal and less weak than the nine-month figure suggests. Free cash flow was negative at USD 36.9 million in the nine months of 2026, yet FY2025 free cash flow was USD 247.9 million and trailing free cash flow is USD 221.5 million, because the fourth quarter of 2025 alone produced about USD 321.2 million of operating cash flow as working capital reversed. The first nine months absorbed a Shintech payment of about USD 114 million, so the fourth quarter of 2026 decides whether the pattern repeats, and the issuer guides the fourth quarter lower than the third.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate until the covenant relief period ends. Cash of USD 214.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 1,029.6 million total USD 1,244.4 million against USD 1,134.3 million of debt due through 2029, and nothing falls due before November 2027. The receivables facility has only USD 34.0 million of spare capacity limited by its borrowing base, so it is not a reserve, and the revolver and the term loan both mature in March 2030.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The test is the end of covenant relief, no later than 2027-09-30. The credit agreement carries a net leverage ceiling and an interest coverage floor that were relaxed in February 2026, and the ratio levels are not printed, so the headroom cannot be measured; the issuer states compliance and no borrowing limit at 2026-09-30. If the merger closes in the first quarter of 2027 the new facility replaces these terms, so the merger is the planned way past the cliff, and a delay would leave tighter covenants against leverage above the FY2025 level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings concentration is moving from chemicals to Winchester. Chlor Alkali Products and Vinyls was 47.85% of nine-month sales against 55.28% a year earlier, its sales fell 14.17% and its segment earnings fell USD 190.6 million, with the Freeport vinyl chloride monomer outage costing USD 72.2 million, while Winchester sales rose 14.14% against an order backlog of USD 1,331 million. Winchester therefore props up cash flow while commodity chemical pricing stays weak, but about 13% of FY2025 sales are to the U.S. government and the fourth quarter is seasonally weakest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and financial policy are average, with no sponsor. The dividend of USD 0.20 per share a quarter continues, repurchases are not printed for 2026 and USD 1,948.9 million of authority remains, so the board can restart distributions at any time while leverage is elevated. Ratings are Fitch BB+ on Rating Watch Positive, Moody's Ba2 with a Negative outlook and Standard & Poor's BB on Credit Watch Developing, a split that followed the merger announcement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The best case against a cautious view is that the nine-month numbers overstate the weakness, which also qualifies the earlier statement that the dividend runs against negative free cash flow, true for nine months only. FY2025 free cash flow was positive after dividends, trailing free cash flow after dividends is USD 130.4 million, the issuer's own adjusted net leverage of 5.2x would fall toward 5.10x or 4.92x if the guided fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 80 million to USD 100 million were delivered with net debt unchanged, and after the merger announcement one agency moved to a positive watch and another to a developing watch. A first quarter 2027 closing on the stated facility, with combined leverage no higher than Olin's today, would move the view to average. A further fall in chemicals earnings, a repeat Freeport outage, an adverse appeal in the Shintech case or a closing that slips past the relief period would move it to weak.

fields.value: The main credit strength is liquidity and maturity structure. Cash and the undrawn revolver of USD 1,244.4 million cover the first maturity, a USD 465.0 million receivables facility due in 2027, about 2.68x, and the revolver, term loan and 2030 notes fall due in 2030 or later, so refinancing pressure arrives only after the covenant relief and merger milestones.

fields.value: A second strength is Winchester, whose nine-month sales rose 14.14%, whose segment earnings rose to USD 77.1 million from USD 67.1 million and whose backlog of USD 1,331 million provides visibility, which cushions weak chemical earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third strength is scale and integration: the largest chlor alkali capacity in North America by the issuer's own account, captive chlorine outlets in epoxy and chlorinated organics, and a diversified product list, which spreads fixed cost and gives more than one outlet for the same electrolysis output.

fields.value: The main weakness is leverage against falling earnings, with net leverage of 7.76x on reported EBITDA and trailing interest cover of 2.12x, which leaves little room for another outage or price decline.

fields.value: A second weakness is concentration of operating risk at Freeport and in commodity chemicals, where an outage cost USD 72.2 million in nine months and subsidized Asian competition keeps epoxy and caustic pricing under pressure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third weakness is cash claims outside the debt and a distribution that does not flex: the Shintech judgment, environmental liabilities of USD 156.8 million and dividends of USD 68.3 million in nine months all call on cash while covenant relief is temporary.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Olin is a vertically integrated chlor alkali, vinyls and epoxy producer with a leading U.S. ammunition business, and its sales are 54.34% chlor alkali and vinyls, 20.23% epoxy and 25.43% Winchester in FY2025. About 32.37% of sales are outside the United States, no customer exceeds 10% of sales, and all three segments are capital intensive, so cash generation depends on keeping fixed-cost plants full at acceptable prices. The company is widely held with no sponsor, so financial policy is set by the board and the creditor risk is the dividend and the merger, not an owner's recapitalisation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is average. Winchester has contracted backlog and a U.S. Army plant contract, while chlor alkali and epoxy sell at commodity prices that fell: chemicals sales are cyclical and tied to the Electrochemical Unit price, and management says it prioritises unit margin over volume, which protects price but gives up sales. Group sales were down 0.84% in the nine months with volume lost to the end of the Blue Water Alliance trading venture and the Freeport outage.

fields.value: Margin resilience is weak. Gross margin was 8.25% in the nine months of 2026 against 9.19% a year earlier, and the issuer's reported EBITDA margin fell with it. Electricity is the largest raw material, about three quarters of it from natural gas or hydroelectric sources, and about 73% of salt is internal supply, which helps cost but leaves earnings exposed to power and natural gas prices, which the third quarter report cites as a cost headwind.

fields.value: Capital intensity is high but flexible at the margin. Capital spending is guided to about USD 200 million for 2026, against depreciation and amortization of about USD 470 million, so the company is spending well under its depreciation and cutting from USD 226.3 million in FY2025, which preserves cash but defers asset renewal. EBITDA converted to free cash flow at 45.54% in FY2025 and at a negative 9.53% in the nine months of 2026, and cash interest alone absorbs 47.17% of trailing reported EBITDA.

fields.value: Rivalry is the force that matters most. The issuer describes global overcapacity, low-priced imports across the epoxy range and subsidized Asian exports, and the owner of a large North American competitor changed in January 2026, so price discipline in chlor alkali and epoxy is outside Olin's control and caps margin recovery. Buyer power is limited by a spread of customers with none above 10% of sales, and supplier power is a risk because the issuer relies on a limited number of suppliers for specified feedstock and services and on third-party transportation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory and policy factors are material to credit. Environmental liabilities of USD 156.8 million at 2026-09-30 are a long-dated cash claim, the Section 45V hydrogen tax credit supported earnings by USD 5.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 against USD 32.0 million a year earlier, and U.S. government contracts carry standard termination rights. Social and technology factors are not primary credit drivers on the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are liquidity, maturities beyond 2027, Winchester and integration, the weaknesses are leverage, Freeport concentration, commodity exposure and cash claims outside the debt, the opportunities are a merger-date facility and recovery in chemicals pricing, and the threats are covenant tightening in 2027, a failed merger and a loss on appeal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is strong on capacity, since the issuer reports the largest chlor alkali capacity in North America, although current earnings are weak. Competitive advantage is average, because integration lowers cost but commodity pricing sets returns. Business diversification is average, with three segments but chemicals still 47.85% of nine-month sales. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because spending was cut but depreciation and fixed cost dominate. Margin stability is weak, free cash flow stability is weak because of the swing between the nine-month and annual results, ability to refinance is average because maturities run to 2029 and beyond but leverage is high and ratings are a notch or more below investment grade, liquidity is average, and financial policy and governance is average. Overall the profile is average to weak, with a deteriorating trend in 2026 and a recovery case that rests on the fourth quarter and on the merger.

fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the headwinds are elevated year-end customer destocking, higher feedstock costs, subsidized Asian exports and planned turnarounds, which the issuer says will push the fourth quarter below the third, with adjusted EBITDA guided to USD 80 million to USD 100 million. The tailwinds are normal operations at the vinyl chloride monomer plant, a recovering epoxy segment, Winchester backlog and the merger. Over three to five years the cost savings programme the issuer calls Beyond250 and a larger combined company are claimed benefits that are management language and are not quantified in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with a second outage at Freeport or a deeper year-end destocking in chlor alkali, which cuts chemicals sales and margin in the fourth quarter and into the first half of 2027. Lower earnings reduce operating cash flow just as the Shintech appeal, environmental spending and the USD 0.20 quarterly dividend continue, so net borrowing rises and trailing adjusted leverage stays above 5x. The first financial break is not liquidity but the covenant tests: if they bind before relief ends, revolver and receivables availability shrink while USD 465.0 million is due in November 2027. Management levers are capital spending, the dividend, the paused repurchases and merger timing. Liquidity of USD 1,244.4 million appears sufficient to avoid distress through 2027 without covenant limits, so the observable triggers are a closing that slips, a failed refinancing of the receivables facility and any restriction on borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Olin presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, integration, Winchester and a maturity wall that starts in 2027, but credit quality is constrained by leverage of 5.21x on adjusted EBITDA and 7.76x on reported EBITDA and by exposure to Freeport and to commodity chemicals pricing. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because of the seasonal working capital swing and cash claims outside the debt. Refinancing capacity depends on the merger closing and on the covenant terms that follow it. The primary downside path is a further earnings decline reaching the end of covenant relief. A definitive opinion needs the executed credit agreement, Huntsman's financial statements and the proxy statement. The top risk is covenant tightening in 2027 against elevated leverage.
